raw_response:
I farm in Quzhou County on the North China Plain, so I will keep to the system I know best: winter wheat followed by summer maize. That fits our climate, the timing of the rains, and the kind of land and work I can manage steadily through the year. At the start of the growing season, my winter wheat is already in the field, so I will put my effort into topdressing, watering at the key stages, and keeping weeds, aphids, and disease under control without spraying too often. After wheat harvest, I will sow summer maize quickly so it can catch the heat and moisture of the rainy season. I will use improved seed, moderate fertilizer, a few irrigations when needed, and rotary tillage because it is simpler and cheaper for me than deep ploughing every season. I will focus on stable yield and lower risk rather than chasing the highest output.
